For each residue shift, norm attainment is equivalent to a maximal weight. Both counterexamples are verified by exact telescoping and tail bounds; hyponormality is exactly monotone weights and forces eventual constancy when the maximum is reached. 11538 exact rational supplementary tests passed. Infinite statements rely on these complete arguments, not truncations.

value.rationale: Determines a natural complete classification of stability under operator powers for all bounded strictly positive unilateral weights. A power can create extra reducing subspaces, so norm attainment of the original does not control the power; conversely a power can regain the stronger all-reducing-subspace property even when the original fails. The two opposite examples establish a genuine boundary, while eventual flatness of hyponormal beta shifts identifies a stable subclass. This solves the full power-membership decision problem on a standard infinite-dimensional operator class, beyond a one-off negative example.
